entries.reason: DerivedRasterContainer is one fail-closed versioned binary-format boundary: it binds fixed header parsing, bounded geometry arithmetic, pixel and payload digests, adaptive row filtering, LZFSE compression and exact RGB reconstruction. Keeping those operations together prevents a serializer, parser or decompressor from accepting different schema or length rules. The type remains package-only and is not connected to the default load path; extraction becomes mandatory if another format, compression backend or independently released artifact reader appears.

entries.reason: FetchStage remains the single transaction and admission owner for ordinary and live transport: fetch identity, task-local versus shared execution, bounded retry, priority propagation, namespace cancellation, progress-qualified completion handoff and the one configured permit pool. Live MJPEG enters through one package method that emits the same redacted fetch diagnostics and invokes only a transport-declared progress-only capability under that existing pool. The capability returns byte/digest/metrics completion without transferring parser, playback, cache, staging or UI authority into FetchStage. Splitting this call into an independent owner would duplicate the permit pool or allow ordinary and long-lived requests to exceed the configured aggregate concurrency ceiling.

entries.reason: HTTPImageResponseProcessor owns one HTTP representation transaction: response validation, cache disposition, transport identity binding, original commit ordering and delivery of verified bytes. Progressive preparations are adopted only after the owning subscriber has observed progress and the candidate digest and byte count equal the completed body; a subscriber that received a shared response without progress closes its empty finalization and safely performs the ordinary full-body decode. Splitting these paths would duplicate the 200/304 commit and namespace barriers.

authorization-aware cache decisions
representation commit barriers
verified-byte and progressive-preparation delivery handoff

entries.reason: SharedTaskRegistry is one actor state machine covering subscription cohorts, effective priority, completion visibility, orphan handoff leases and cancellation tombstones. Completed entries remain joinable only inside the active cohort and can be explicitly invalidated before a fresh cache-observation transaction. Absolute monotonic expiry and lazy admission checks make timers cleanup optimizations rather than correctness dependencies. Keeping entry, invalidation, tombstone, lease identity, completion and join transitions in one actor preserves the linearization boundary and prevents ABA races.

modules.reason: FoveaCore remains the Fovea-owned policy and orchestration layer for request identity, geometry, bounded fetch/decode execution, namespace lifecycle, shared work and diagnostics. The reviewed 81-file set contains separately factored static/progressive image orchestration, default-off derived raster support, deterministic decoder-neutral animation playback, and package-only live MJPEG transport/playback. The new authorized encoded animation seam preserves ContentID, exact request execution identity, selected representation identity and namespace generation across cache/network loading, decoder preparation and runtime registration; generation floors prevent post-revocation static or live registration races. FoveaCore still does not import platform UI or own an ImageIO animation implementation, and the public/default static image path remains unchanged. Extraction becomes mandatory before animation is an independently released public product surface or a new module can own these policies without importing FoveaCore back.

pipeline orchestration, deadline scheduling and shared ordinary/live resource admission
